source_text: Ταῦτα ἡ πλάνη ἐπᾴδουσα ἔτι, καὶ τοιαῦτα συμβουλεύει· Τί πράττεις, ὦ οὗτος, καὶ οὐ τρυφᾷς, οὐδὲ ἐμφορῇ μὲν ἐδεσμάτων παντοίων, οἴνου δὲ ὑπερεμπίπλασαι; Οὐκ αἰσθάνῃ, ὡς ἐκ Θεοῦ ταυτὶ δέδοται πρὸς ἀπόλαυσιν ἀνεπικώλυτον; Περιβαλοῦ ἐσθῆτα νεόπλυτον, καὶ μύρῳ τὴν κεφαλὴν χρισάμενος, ὅρα τὴν γυναῖκα ταύτην, κἀκείνην δὲ ματαίως τὸν μάταιον πάρελθε βίον; Ἕτερον γὰρ οὐδὲν ὑπολείπεταί σοι παρὰ ταῦτα, οὐκ ἐνθάδε, οὐδὲ μετὰ θάνατον. Ἀλλὰ πράττε τὰ προστυχόντα. Οὔτε γὰρ λογισμὸν σέ τις τούτων εἰσπράξεται· οὔθ᾽ ὅλως γινώσκεται ἐκτὸς ἀνθρώπων τὰ ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων γινόμενα. Ἅιδης δὲ, ὅ τί ποτε καὶ ἔστιν, εἰς ὃν ἀπιέναι λεγόμεθα, σοφίας καὶ αἰσθήσεως ἀμοιρεῖ. Ταῦτα μὲν οἱ μάταιοι.
thought_title: Error still singing its counsel to indulge
orientation: The voice of the foolish error is still speaking and urging indulgence before it is answered.
pass_a_gloss: These things the error still chanting sings, and it counsels such things as these: What are you doing, O you there, and you do not live soft and you do not stuff yourself with a filling of foods of every kind, and you do not fill yourself beyond measure with wine? Do you not perceive that these things have been given from God for enjoyment that is not hindered? Put on clothing newly washed, and with your head anointed with ointment, look at this woman, and with her in vain pass through the vain life? For nothing different is left remaining for you besides these things, neither here nor after death. But do the things that come to hand. For no one will exact from you a reckoning for these things; nor at all are the things done by men known outside men. And Hades, whatever indeed it also is, into which we are said to go away, has no share in wisdom and perception. These things on the one hand say the vain.

choices.why: keeps the continuing singing image and the prior foolish reasoning as speaker
rejected: the delusion still singing its spell

choices.why: keeps three distinct verbs of excess and their active second person force

pass_b_english: The error is still chanting, and its counsel runs like this: "What are you doing, fellow, that you do not live softly, stuff yourself with every kind of food, and fill yourself with wine beyond measure? Can you not see that God has given these things for enjoyment that is not hindered? (Ecclesiastes 9:7)"

"Put on freshly washed clothing, anoint your head with oil, look at this woman, and that one too, and vainly pass through this vain life. (Ecclesiastes 9:8; Ecclesiastes 9:9) For nothing else is left for you besides these things, neither here nor after death. So do whatever comes to hand. (Ecclesiastes 9:10)"

"For no one will exact an account of these things from you. What is done by human beings is not known at all outside human beings. And Hades, whatever it is, to which we are said to go, has no share in wisdom or perception. (Ecclesiastes 9:10)" That, on the one hand, is what the vain say.
notes: The clause with κἀκείνην δὲ ματαίως is uncertain in exact connection; glossed as with her in vain, without inventing further text.

problems.quote: look to this woman, and vainly pass through this vain life with her.
problems.source_quote: ὅρα τὴν γυναῖκα ταύτην, κἀκείνην δὲ ματαίως τὸν μάταιον πάρελθε βίον
problems.why: The source says 'this woman, and that one too'. The English drops κἀκείνην and adds 'with her'. That turns the plural into one woman as companion.
problems.fix: look at this woman, and that one too, and vainly pass through this vain life.
